results.reason: Issue 3 contrasts Sched. §1.1 (ship date) with MSA §1.3 (delivery at Rochester). It explains that lateness is measured by ship date, which undercuts §5.2 remedies. It also covers risk passing at shipment and invoicing on shipment, which starts the payment clock early.
The fix section recommends conforming the Schedule's 'Delivery Date' definition to MSA §1.3 (delivery at Rochester) and adding an order-of-precedence clause.

Issue 1 identifies MSA §4.3's worldwide, all-housings exclusivity versus Term Sheet §§3.1–3.3 (Series 7 Housings, US only). It explains the lock-in and the bar on buying elsewhere, and recommends narrowing to Series 7 in the US. Non-U.S. plants are not named explicitly, but the worldwide lock-in is addressed.

Issue 5.1 notes §15.2 lets Supplier assign freely while Customer needs consent. It flags the risk of a competing assignee holding Harlow's Specifications under exclusivity. It recommends mutual consent or, at minimum, a no-competitor bar and a change-of-control termination right.

Issue 2 explains that the Amendment restates §11.2 to exclude only willful misconduct, so gross negligence and the IP indemnity fall under the 12-month-fees cap. It recommends restoring the original §11.2(a)–(c).
The memo states the cap is fees paid in the prior 12 months (§11.1). It lists the original §11.2 exclusions as gross negligence, willful misconduct and the §10.1 IP indemnity.
The memo states the Term Sheet exclusivity covers Series 7 Housings in the US only and uses that as the baseline for comparing the MSA clause.
New York law (MSA §16.1) is stated in the header, and the memo includes NY-law points and assumptions. The UCC references are real statutes and are flagged as to be confirmed. No cases are cited.

The memo is organized for the partner with a bottom line and issues ranked by importance. Each issue gives Where, Why it matters and Fix, and there is a separate section on assumptions and facts needed.

The Term Sheet is used only as evidence of intent and leverage. The 3-year term and 45-day payment terms are not treated as defects in themselves; the payment point is tied to the Delivery Date conflict.
Exclusivity and assignment are attributed to the correct sections, with the correct party benefiting. The legal points are flagged as unverified or to be confirmed.
